balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

receivablesFleet.title: Loan & lease receivables vs owned fleet
receivablesFleet.content:
Loan & lease receivables is the outstanding financing book from vessels placed with customers under finance leases and loans -- the core earning asset of a ship-leasing business, economically equivalent to a bank's loan book. Vessels / PP&E is the fleet the company owns and operates directly (or leases out under operating leases) rather than financing through a receivable.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the mix between the two shows how the balance sheet is deployed -- receivables ran down from HK$23.7bn in FY2023 to HK$18.5bn in FY2025 while owned vessels fell from HK$16.4bn to HK$15.5bn, consistent with a maturing/runoff book rather than aggressive new financing.

What to watch:

  • Growth in receivables signals new financing-lease volume; a shrinking book signals runoff or weaker origination
  • Owned vessels carry residual-value and charter-rate risk that a financing receivable does not
  • Both are balance-sheet (FY-only) figures -- not reported at the half-year

impairmentLoanLease.title: Net impairment on loan & lease receivables
impairmentLoanLease.content:
The net impairment charge (or reversal, shown negative) taken against the loan & lease receivables book in the period -- the credit-quality read-through for a ship lessor, equivalent to a bank's loan-loss provision.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the charge spiked to HK$447m in FY2024 (its worst year in the series) before easing back to HK$79m in FY2025; FY2020-FY2021 instead booked net reversals, meaning the book was recovering provisions rather than taking new charges.

What to watch:

  • A rising charge against a shrinking receivables book means credit quality is deteriorating faster than the book itself
  • Compare against counterparty concentration and charter-market conditions in the filings -- shipping is cyclical and impairments often lag freight-rate downturns

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For CSSC (Hong Kong) Shipping Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
